headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-flow from a browser-capable, networked support agent into a non-networked audio model; other risks are limited by B's read-only, no-tool profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can run browsers, use broad network egress, and invoke runtime-injected MCPs/hooks; Agent B has no tool use or input provenance controls beyond command-line usage. If A's outputs are copied into B's prompts or transcripts, malicious content from A can steer B. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Agent A content is forwarded into Agent B prompts or transcripts without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF a shared clipboard, message queue, or file bridge is added between them, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable any automatic copy/paste bridge between agents.
Strip instructions from A's outputs before passing text to B.
Use a fixed prompt template for B that treats A output as untrusted data.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all A-to-B handoffs.
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer that removes imperative language from A outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches session history, project code, and provider auth data and has broad egress; Agent B cannot read files, use the network, or handle secrets. There is no shared workspace or direct file bridge in the profiles, so leakage from A to B is not a default path. The main concern is manual transfer of sensitive A output into B, which is limited blast radius.
conditions: IF operators paste A's sensitive outputs into B, B may echo them in transcripts.
IF a shared workspace is introduced later, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets from A into B prompts.
Redact auth data and session history before handoff.
Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.
requires-engineering: add access controls for any shared storage.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can spawn subprocesses and use multiple instances; Agent B cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Because B lacks mutable capabilities, there is no meaningful write-write conflict on shared resources in the current profiles. Any conflict would require adding a shared writable surface not present here.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory is added and B gains write access, contention becomes possible.
IF A is configured to manage the same git repo as another writer, conflicts may occur.
mitigations: Keep B read-only.
Do not grant B filesystem or git write permissions.
Run A and B in separate directories.
requires-engineering: add file locks for any shared mutable repo.
requires-engineering: serialize writes through one orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can browse and call external APIs, so it may generate unverified facts or summaries that Agent B could transcribe or act on. Agent B has no built-in verification or tool authority, but if its outputs are treated as authoritative downstream, errors can cascade across work products. The pathway is plausible from profiles alone, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Agent B is instructed to reuse A's outputs without verification, errors can propagate.
IF downstream systems trust B's transcript as ground truth, the cascade widens.
mitigations: Require B to cite source text for any factual claim.
Compare A outputs against a second source before use.
Mark A-generated content as unverified in B prompts.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between A and B.
requires-engineering: block B from issuing actions based solely on A output.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles provider auth data, installation identifiers, and session history and has broad egress; Agent B only touches audio/speech and has no network or file access. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, and B is not a data-transmitting service here. The only compliance concern is limited manual transfer of A data into B, so low fits.
conditions: IF regulated data from A is manually transcribed into B, compliance review is needed.
IF B is deployed with a different retention policy than A, mismatch risk increases.
mitigations: Do not route secrets through B.
Keep regulated data out of A-to-B handoffs.
Document retention for any transcripts.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated fields.
requires-engineering: segregate logs by data class.
